overall: The AG found the Selectboard violated the Open Meeting Law by holding its February 26 and March 12, 2025 meetings at Town Hall, which was not accessible (parking and elevator), and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Feb 26 meeting at Town Hall allegedly inaccessible because the building lacks compliant handicap parking.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, based on that decision, we find that the February 26 meeting also was insufficiently accessible in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: March 12 meeting allegedly inaccessible because the Town Hall elevator was out of service, which the Board does not dispute.
allegations.key_passage: The Board does not dispute that the elevator was out of service during the March 12 meeting and that without a working elevator the meeting location was inaccessible to individuals with mobility impairments.

allegations.summary: Board argued that offering Zoom access cured the elevator problem; the AG rejected this as a defense to the ADA location requirement.
allegations.key_passage: The Board has since acknowledged—and we reiterate—that offering a Zoom option for a meeting that is otherwise held in person does not obviate the need to hold meetings in ADA-compliant locations.

allegations.summary: Complainant asserted that accessibility barriers meant he missed or could not fully take part in public comment at the two meetings.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation, but rather gives the chair of the public body discretion to decide whether to permit public comment during a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised earlier elevator outages at Town Hall at prior meetings more than 30 days before the complaint was filed.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review allegations regarding meetings that took place more than 30 days prior to the filing of the complaint.

allegations.summary: Board did not respond in writing to the complaint, filed March 24, until the AG's office inquired; noted in a footnote as a reminder of the 14-business-day rule.
allegations.key_passage: The complainant provided email communications showing he sent the complaint to the Board on March 24; the Board did not respond until our office inquired as to the status.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
